brief.industry_meta: Fleet Electrification · Electric Buses, Charging & Grid Storage
brief.deck: Zenobē, the London fleet-electrification and grid-battery operator owned by KKR and Infracapital, secured c.£980M of new financing on 15 June 2026 to put 1,200 more electric buses on UK and Irish roads, taking capital raised past £3.2B, then added a $400M Australasian platform and a German acquisition within six weeks.
brief.the_case_p1: Zenobē announced on 15 June that 22 banks, NatWest, Lloyds, Santander and Aviva among them, had committed c.£980M to its UK and Ireland electric-fleet facility: £480M of long-dated term debt, a £400M capex line and £100M of ancillaries. Capital raised since 2017 now exceeds £3.2B. Nine days later it closed a $400M platform for zero-emission fleets in Australia and New Zealand, and on 27 July it bought Bavaria's sdp energie with a 1.75 GW German battery pipeline. KKR and Infracapital have been joint majority owners since a c.£870M equity round in September 2023.
brief.the_case_p2: This is a company that has already paid for motorsport in kind: its second-life bus-battery powerskids were Extreme E's official energy-storage supply from the series' first season to its final event in October 2025. With Extreme E gone, that budget line is orphaned. Zenobē now sells fleet electrification to bus operators in Britain, Europe, North America and Australasia, and the buyers it needs are transport authorities, fleet owners and the banks that fund them.
brief.why_now_callout: <font name='Poppins-Bold' size='9'>WHY NOW</font>  Three financings in six weeks reset the marketing calendar. Formula E's GEN4 era opens in Jeddah on 18 December, and the London E-Prix moves to Brands Hatch on 29-30 May 2027: the reigning champions' home race, forty miles from Zenobē's London office, is the natural launch stage.
brief.why_team_para: Jaguar TCS Racing are the reigning Teams' World Champions, run from Kidlington, Oxfordshire, and committed to GEN4 through 2030. The roster in the sponsor table is TCS as title partner and Castrol; there is no fleet, charging or storage brand, so the lane is open. A British electrification operator on the British champions' car at a British home race is the cleanest story on the grid.
brief.value_content: MODE A - operational. Zenobē's second-life battery powerskids powered five Extreme E paddocks; at Jaguar they can carry garage and hospitality load at European rounds where event-power rules allow, cutting generator diesel on camera. Off track, Zenobē electrifies the team's Kidlington depot and support fleet under its fleet-as-a-service model. Commercially: Brands Hatch hospitality for transport authorities, fleet owners and lenders, and an Official Fleet Electrification Partner designation.
brief.deal_arch_para: Entry as Official Fleet Electrification and Energy Storage Partner. <font name='Poppins-Bold' size='9.5'>THREE YEARS</font>, Seasons 13-15 (2026/27 to 2028/29), from the GEN4 debut through the first two Brands Hatch home races. Estimated £1-2M a year, part-payable in powerskid supply and depot electrification. Scope: sidepod branding, Brands Hatch and Berlin hospitality, paddock-power content, and a bus-operator guest programme.
brief.decision_maker_bio: Weir joined Zenobē as CEO in 2025; a first Formula E partnership is his call. Path: Steven Meersman, Co-Founder and Director, EV Fleet; Tim Boothman, Chief Commercial Officer, Electric Fleet; Iain Wetherall, CFO, formerly CFO of Wizz Air. No chief marketing officer is listed.
brief.opening_angle_intro: Lead with Extreme E and Brands Hatch.
brief.opening_angle_quote: “Donald, Zenobē powered Extreme E's paddock for five seasons and that series has gone. The reigning Formula E champions race at Brands Hatch next May with no fleet or storage partner on the car. 25 minutes to see what the seat costs?”
score_cells: Trigger 15 Jun is twelve weeks old; GEN4 opener in December, Brands Hatch in May.
£3.2B raised, KKR-owned; mostly project debt, revenue not public.
Fleet electrification is Formula E's own story; British; Extreme E precedent.
No listing or deadline; the home-race debut is the soft trigger.
MODE A: paddock power and depot electrification; open lane.
risks: The £980M is bank debt for buses and chargers, not a marketing budget, and the company's revenue is not public.
Price the entry at £1-2M with in-kind supply; the Extreme E precedent shows the budget line exists.
Event power at an E-Prix is the championship's remit; team-level powerskid use needs Formula E's approval.
Start with garage, hospitality and depot load, which need no approval; add trackside supply later.
brief.bottom_line: £980M closed in June, a $400M Australasian platform and a German acquisition inside six weeks, five seasons of paying for motorsport at Extreme E, and a home race at Brands Hatch in May: Zenobē has the budget, the habit and the stage. The fleet and storage lane at Jaguar TCS Racing is open.

why_now.label: Trigger
why_now.text: On 15 June 2026 Zenobē announced c.£980M of new financing for its UK and Ireland electric-fleet facility, the facility's third round: £480M of new long-dated term commitments, a £400M capital-expenditure facility and £100M of ancillaries from 22 banks including NatWest, Lloyds, Santander and Aviva. It funds more than 1,200 new electric buses and their charging over three years and takes capital raised since 2017 past £3.2B.

why_now.label: Three financings in six weeks
why_now.text: Nine days after the UK round, Zenobē closed a $400M platform for zero-emission heavy-vehicle fleets across Australia and New Zealand, seeded with four operating depots. On 27 July it bought Bavaria's sdp energie and with it a 1.75 GW pipeline of transmission-connected battery projects in Germany. Combined with the €325M European facility, the company expects to support up to 5,000 electric buses by 2028. A company scaling on four continents at once is at the point where a global brand gets built.

why_now.label: A motorsport budget with nowhere to go
why_now.text: Zenobē was Extreme E's Official Energy Storage Supplier from the series' first season in 2021, powering remote paddocks with powerskids built from second-life bus batteries. Extreme E ran its farewell event in October 2025. The company has proved it will fund motorsport and has just lost the property it funded; Formula E is the obvious successor and the powerskid story transfers intact.

why_now.label: Calendar window
why_now.text: Formula E's GEN4 era opens with the Jeddah double-header on 18-19 December 2026. The London E-Prix moves from ExCeL to Brands Hatch on 29-30 May 2027, a new home for the reigning champions' home race, about forty miles from Zenobē's London office and within reach of every UK bus operator it sells to.

why_team.label: The open lane
why_team.text: Jaguar TCS Racing's roster in the sponsor table is TCS as title partner and Castrol, with Jaguar as powertrain supplier and parent; the team's own partner page adds Wolfspeed, Reflo, OpenText, Dow and Chase. None is a fleet-electrification, charging or energy-storage brand. Official Fleet Electrification and Energy Storage Partner is a clean category at a team-partner price.

why_team.label: The champions
why_team.text: Jaguar TCS Racing won the 2025/26 Teams' World Championship at the London finale with Mitch Evans and António Félix da Costa, 17 points clear of Porsche, and is committed to the GEN4 era through 2030 under team principal Ian James. A partner joining for Season 13 joins the reigning champions in the first year of a new car.

why_team.label: British on British
why_team.text: Zenobē is London-headquartered and Britain's largest owner and operator of transmission-connected batteries; Jaguar TCS Racing is run from Kidlington, Oxfordshire. The Brands Hatch home race puts both in front of the transport authorities, bus operators and lenders that decide Zenobē's UK pipeline.

why_team.label: Fleet customers in common
why_team.text: Jaguar's parent sells vehicles to the same fleet buyers Zenobē electrifies. A joint proposition to fleet owners, vehicle plus depot plus charging plus finance, is a commercial programme the team's parent can carry beyond the racetrack.

value.label: Operational workstream (Mode A)
value.text: Second-life battery powerskids for the team's garage and hospitality load at European rounds, subject to the championship's event-power rules, replacing generator diesel with a visible, on-camera story. Zenobē ran exactly this for five Extreme E seasons.

value.label: Depot and fleet electrification
value.text: Zenobē's fleet-as-a-service model, vehicles, chargers, batteries and finance, applied to the team's Kidlington base and support fleet, giving the champions a measured emissions reduction they can report and Zenobē a reference site.

value.label: Commercial lift for the team
value.text: Zenobē brings bus operators, transport authorities, city officials and the 22 banks behind its facility to Brands Hatch and Berlin; a guest list that overlaps with the public-sector and financial audience TCS and Chase already court.

value.label: What the team gives back
value.text: Official Fleet Electrification and Energy Storage Partner designation, sidepod branding, Brands Hatch and Berlin hospitality, paddock-power content, and driver access for Zenobē's customer events in the UK, Europe, North America and Australasia.

ruled_out.reason: The owner, Envision Group, runs its own battery and storage businesses (Envision Energy, Envision AESC): a storage operator on that car competes with the owner. Paysafe became title partner on 14 August 2026.

ruled_out.team: Lola Yamaha ABT Formula E Team
ruled_out.reason: Shell is the energy partner and Shell's fleet-charging business is a direct rival.
TotalEnergies, which sells fleet charging, holds the energy lane; DS Automobiles leaves after Season 12 and Penske's Season 13 entry was unregistered at the last report.
TDK, a battery and component maker, is the official technology partner; German team, no UK home-race story.
Open lane and a US audience, but Zenobē's core market and home race are British; better kept for US-led prospects.

ruled_out.team: Nissan Formula E Team · Mahindra Racing · Cupra Kiro · Citroën Racing
ruled_out.reason: Open but not chosen: no champion status, no British home story and no comparable fleet-customer overlap.

extended.ask: A 25-minute call with Donald Weir before the Jeddah opener to confirm the financing and the Extreme E budget history on the record, agree a Brands Hatch announcement window, and size an Official Fleet Electrification and Energy Storage Partner entry at Jaguar TCS Racing for Seasons 13-15.

# Zenobē → Jaguar TCS Racing — verification log (N° 130, 5 Sep 2026)

Built in-session at no API cost with Claude as scanner, verifier and writer through the
pipeline's injectable stages; the calendar table, sponsor table, 13-rule audit and the 2-page
render ran as code. `zenobe.run.json` is the case record.

**Sandbox limitation, stated plainly:** direct fetches of zenobe.com, media.jaguar.com,
fiaformulae.com, prnewswire.com, energy-storage.news and the trade press were blocked by the
egress proxy. Every claim below was checked against the search summary of the primary page named
as the evidence URL. Treat every VERIFIED line as REPORTED until a person opens the link.
Confidence is MEDIUM and the footer reads VERIFY BEFORE CIRCULATION.

## The trigger, corrected

The desk row dated the financing 17 Jun (electrive's publication date). Zenobē's own release and
route-one.net date it **15 Jun 2026**, which is the `signal_date` (82 days before the row's date,
inside the 90-day window). The row's '$400M platform for Australia/NZ' was announced on 24 Jun,
after the trigger, and is presented as a follow-on, not part of the trigger. The £980M is **debt**
(bank facilities), not equity: the brief and the first risk row say so.
